title: How AI agents work: build one from scratch
kicker: Model, context, tools and a loop
blurb: Builds an agent piece by piece: a model that predicts text, a context list, tools, a loop, then memory, skills, sub-agents and autonomy.
description: The film builds an agent from nothing. It starts with a model that only predicts tokens, shows that a chatbot's memory is a list the program resends, and adds tools and a loop. It then covers context limits and compaction, memory, skills, sub-agents, heartbeats for autonomy, and the safety risks that come with more power.
takeaways: A language model only predicts the next token; a chatbot's memory is a message list that the program sends again every time.
Giving the model tool descriptions lets it ask the program to act, and a loop of ask, act and ask again makes an agent.
The context holds everything and is resent every step, so agents compact older parts, and deciding what to keep is the art.
Skills load full instructions only when a task matches, and sub-agents return only a short report to keep the main context clean.
More power means more risk, so treat what an agent reads as data, give least access and ask a human before irreversible steps.
